 O R D E R

The accused in C.C. No.158 of 1996 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class- II, Kannur filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) read with Sections 7(i) and 7(v) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class- II, Kannur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.
The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 4.12.1995, PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 24 pieces of ice fruit from the shop of the first accused.
The accused Nos.1 and 2 were running the shop.
The third accused was the licensee of the said shop.
After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.
The Public Analyst filed Ext. P11 report stating that the sample contained non-permitted coal tar dye Rhodamine-B and artificial sweetener saccharine and therefore, the same was adulterated.
Thereafter, on the request of the accused, second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis.
Ext.P14 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item and therefore, it was adulterated.
It was also stated in Ext.P14 certificate that the sample contained non-permitted coal tar dye Rhodamine-B and artificial sweetener saccharine.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts.P1 to P22 were marked for the prosecution.
Ext.D1 was marked for the revision petitioners.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P14 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)

2 (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

sentences.text: Therefore, Ext. P14 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In the result, this Revision Petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) read with Sections 7(i) and 7(v) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the revision petitioners are acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bonds of the revision petitioners stand cancelled and they are set at liberty.

SD/-
B.SUDHEENDRA KUMAR, JUDGE dl/23.3.2016 // True Copy // PA to Judge M.Umesh vs Food Inspector on 21 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104777098/
